why: THE TAX ON THE OTHER HALF OF A WHEEL. Both commanders charge for a wheel's own half — Brallin a counter and a ping per DISCARD, Shabraz a counter per DRAW — and nothing in the 99 charged for the half that refills the OPPONENTS. The model could not see that half either until 2026-09-14, when event_payoffs learned the opponent-draw trigger and the wheel started refilling the opponent seat. IN: Razorkin Needlehead (1 damage to them per draw), Scrawling Crawler (1 life per draw, and it makes them draw), Anje's Ravager (a repeatable DISCARD wheel on a body, attacking every combat). OUT: the three cards engine.json places in no stage — Marketback Walker pays only when it dies, Stromkirk Noble grows only on its own combat damage, Waterbender Ascension needs a fourth quest counter before it draws anything and card-value measured it at +0.000. Priced at 4,000 games seed 5 against a 9.87 ping baseline with 0.12 seed noise: Razorkin +2.46 ping, Scrawling Crawler +1.97, Anje's Ravager +1.84 ping AND +1.81 cards AND +4.30 combat damage. Brass's Tunnel-Grinder was searched, priced at -0.25 and DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — its enter-and-discard is unparsed, so the model cannot see it and a number from it would be about its mana value. EVERY PING FIGURE IS AGAINST ONE SEAT: the model has a single 40-life opponent, so a four-player table pays roughly three times this and these are floors. Objective pinned to the champion's own damage@8 of 30.1335 [29.81, 30.45] read from diagnostic.json at the harness net-change grades on (10,000 games, seed 20260826), immediately before opening.
